name: rietx.background.auto.AIR_SCATTER_TRIGGER
decides: nested-fit gain (cubic vs cubic + 1/2theta on the envelope) above which auto_background declares the air-scatter term
without: auto_background would never (or always) declare instrument.background.air; the caller sees no term
evidence: v0.2: 0.3 sits between 0.85 (synthetic air scatter) and 1e-4 (flat); WP-1130 F7 and #636 show it misses real low-angle rises
provenance: v0.2 (background.diagnose), synthetic patterns only (tests/test_background_auto.py:79-94); failures measured in WP-1130 Finding 7, #636, and the LOW_ANGLE_UNMODELLED docstring (refine.py:8407)
families: synthetic air-scatter and flat patterns (v0.2): verifies only, own synthetic
Ba2FeSbSe5 1.5 K CW neutron: real low-angle tail reads 0.019, trigger misses it (docstring)
synthetic peak-dense synchrotron capillary (#636): 0.0035 with the rise, 0.047 without
failure_case: WP-1130 F7: a genuine 900/(2theta) term reads 0.069 because a cubic already absorbs 1/x over 60 deg; #636: gain set by hump and line density, not the rise
judgement: fails: dissenter is a refiner of a peak-dense synchrotron capillary scan who sees a low-angle rise by eye and wants the term although the gain reads 0.0035; opposite dissenter is a lab Bragg-Brentano user who wants none
note: Inside a pick verb (caller tier), so the pick exception may keep it, but only if the ranking travels with the pick: auto_background returns the Background alone, not diag.air_scatter_gain or the nested-fit scores. See notes.md section 2. A declined term leaves no record field (absence is the record, WP-1454).

name: rietx.background.auto.HUMP_TRIGGER

judgement: fails: dissenter is any refiner shown 0.047 versus 0.043 and told they differ in knot spacing; the statistic does not separate hump from no hump on the measured pair
note: Same pick-exception caveat as AIR_SCATTER_TRIGGER: the score is not returned beside the pick.

name: rietx.background.models.FIXED_RANGE_SLACK_STEPS

name: rietx.background.diagnostics.GHOST_MIN_PARENTS
decides: how many of the strongest lines must carry a ghost candidate at one common ratio before a contamination is reported
without: per-line rule flagged 0.94 Kbeta per pattern, the same as the fake-wavelength control's 1.01: flags at the chance rate
evidence: WP-1442: control (2,656 made-up-wavelength draws) maxes at 4, 0.000 % reach 5; injected Kbeta at r = 0.10 scores >= 6, 0.15 >= 5
provenance: WP-1442 (decided 2026-09-22 with the maintainer); 16 round-robin patterns x 166 control wavelengths

judgement: passes: a line at the Kbeta or W La position of >= 5 of the 8 strongest reflections at one ratio is a beam leak on every account. Dissenter: an indexer whose real reflection coincides with a flagged position loses that line from PeakList.usable; the flag and the line stay in peaks, so it is reversible
note: THE ACTION IS 2003's (indexing): flag_ghosts runs by default in pick_peaks (indexing/pick.py:55 flag_contamination=True, :96, :191) and flagged lines are excluded from PeakList.usable. The GHOST_* constants, _ANODE_MATCH_TOL, _KBETA and _W_LA1 are its thresholds. Only one family for positives; the other 'families' are negative controls. Source declared as monochromator or neutron skips the screen (ghost_searches). Tier-3 mechanical ground fails on count of positive families.

decides: A row whose slack is under 0 by less than this fraction of its block's largest |slack| is on its face, not violated.
evidence: numerical floor: tolerance covering the last-bit disagreement of two association orders; the value of strategy.staged.STEPHENS_CONE_TOL (docstring)
note: Inherits the tier of STEPHENS_CONE_TOL and RESOLUTION_CONE_TOL (strategy/staged.py:1266, 1596), which another reader tiers; 1e-9 is 4.5e6 eps, a margin and not a derived value. Cannot move a reported number beyond 1e-9 relative.

name: rietx.optimize.lm._ROW_ROUNDING
decides: Relative amount by which the box-only step may cross a linear-inequality row and still be taken.
evidence: numerical floor: rounding of the row's own evaluation, 4.5e3 eps, seven decades under the guards' 1e-9 (docstring)
note: Larger crossings take the exact constrained step, so a wrong value costs a solve, not an answer.

name: rietx.optimize.lm._NULL_CURVATURE
decides: Curvature, as a fraction of lambda_max, given to the directions the eigenvalue cut discards when rows must also hold.
evidence: numerical floor: sqrt(eps); at the cut itself three of 1000 random problems stayed rank-deficient, sqrt(eps) left none (docstring)
note: The 1000-problem trial is cited in the comment as 'below'; no test of that name found (grep tests/test_lm_solver.py 2026-10-19).

name: rietx.optimize.lm._POLISH_FEASIBLE
decides: The polished constrained step is kept if it holds every row to this fraction of the row's scale.
evidence: WP-1938 D8: measured on 1000 random synthetic problems; the polish passed on all 898 that crossed a row, worst row -7e-13
provenance: WP-1938 decision D8 (2-11 parameters, column scales 1e-3 to 1e3, up to 29 rows, a fifth rank-deficient).
families: synthetic random problems only, verifies (exact constrained minimiser)
failure_case: The unpolished least-distance point's worst row sat at -1.4e-7 of its scale.
note: Synthetic only, so no real-data family. If the polish fails the least-distance point stands; the outer loop re-measures the real cost, so the effect is a 1e-7 relative step difference.

name: rietx.optimize.lm._POLISH_STATIONARY
decides: The polished step is kept if its gradient is a non-negative combination of the active rows to this fraction of the gradient's scale.
evidence: WP-1938 D8: measured on 1000 random synthetic problems; worst stationarity residual 4e-10
provenance: WP-1938 decision D8 (same 1000 problems).
families: synthetic random problems only, verifies (exact constrained minimiser)
failure_case: As _POLISH_FEASIBLE.
note: Eight decades above the measured worst; a margin, not a derived value.

name: rietx.optimize.lm._EIGEN_CUT_PER_ROW
decides: Eigenvalues of the equilibrated normal matrix below this * max(rows, n) * lambda_max are discarded from the LM step.
evidence: numerical floor: eps*m, the rounding error of one inner product over m terms (Higham 2002 §3.1; docstring)
note: A different cut from PINV_RCOND on the same matrix: for N = 1e4 rows this is ~2e-12 of lambda_max against 1e-15 for the covariance. A direction between them gets no step and a finite huge variance (clash candidate, notes.md). Not applied above BVLS_MAX_COLUMNS (projected CG makes no cut; FAP.XRA Pawley: BVLS Rwp 0.0803 against 0.0782, lm.py:731-735).

name: rietx.optimize.lm.BVLS_MAX_COLUMNS
decides: Largest system the LM step solves exactly by BVLS; above it the step is budgeted projected CG. Also the bound test's exactness limit.
without: Above it BVLS would cost 0.7-3.1 s a solve at 1 500 Pawley columns; the bound test could not know which set is exact (strategy/staged.py:1715-1735 returns None above it).
evidence: WP-1937 and WP-1953: BVLS costs 2-34 ms at 128 columns, 0.13-0.8 s at 400, 10-177 s at 2000; projected CG 0.002-0.64 s on real Pawley systems
provenance: WP-1937 Pawley-shaped synthetic systems; WP-1953 real Pawley systems (FAP.XRA 343 columns, NAC 1 493-1 499).
families: GSAS-II FAP.XRA lab Pawley, verifies (TRF Rwp 0.0782)
APS 11-BM NAC Pawley, verifies (converges every stage, Rwp 0.12620721)
synthetic Pawley-shaped systems, cost only
failure_case: BCCG, the step above the cut until WP-1953, had a positive model value at most lambda > 0 on FAP's 343 columns, up to 6e6 times the best; projected CG's budgeted solve can stop short of a bound (lm.py:324-330).
judgement: none: a cost-driven choice between an exact and a budgeted solver for the same model; no refiner is asked to decide it. The visible consequence is the bound test's route: exact active set up to the cut, residual-cosine conjunction above (staged.py:1715-1760).
note: Not answer-invariant (FAP Pawley 0.0803 BVLS against 0.0782 projected CG), so not the invariant class. The edge is a table + Pawley column count, len(theta)+n_aux > 128 (staged.py:1735), so a 130-parameter table-only fit already takes the other route. Two real families only.

name: rietx.optimize.qpa.BRINDLEY_MU_R_FENCE
decides: mu*R above which a phase is outside Brindley's medium-powder regime (BRINDLEY_OUTSIDE_REGIME).
evidence: Brindley (1945) Phil. Mag. 36, 347: medium powders mu*D <= 0.1, D = 2R; FullProf manual's QPA section gives the same classes (checked: FullProf_Manual.pdf, 0.01 < mD < 0.1)
note: Gates a diagnostic only (qpa.py:312, WP-2005's), and the Brindley correction itself runs only when the caller supplies particle_radius_um (caller). 0.05 = 0.1/2 inherits the 0.1.

name: rietx.optimize.statistics.PINV_RCOND
decides: Relative cut: eigenvalues of the equilibrated normal matrix at or under this * |lambda|max are discarded from every esd.
without: A rounding-level eigenvalue (+-3.5e-15 of the largest on LaB6+cBN, WP-1930) would be inverted as a real direction.
evidence: numerical floor: 1e-15 = 4.5 eps_fp64, numpy.linalg.pinv's own default (checked: numpy 2.5.4 docstring)
note: Practice differs: GSAS-II equilibrates then pinvs at SVDtol = 1e-6 (GSASIIobj.py:20, GSASIImath.HessianLSQ, checked), nine decades looser, and reports the 'SVD zeros'. At 1e-15 a direction GSAS-II would zero gets a huge finite variance here; both flag it. Eigenvalue noise on LaB6+cBN sits within 4x of this cut, so the value is marginal on that fit (WP-1930 handled it by inverting the magnitude). Derived: refine.SCALE_B_SEPARATION_FLOOR = 2*sqrt(PINV_RCOND) and params.parametric.RANK_RTOL = sqrt(PINV_RCOND).

name: rietx.optimize.statistics.COLUMN_SAFE_EXPONENT
decides: Jacobian columns whose largest entry has a binary exponent beyond +-400 are rescaled by an exact power of two before squaring.
without: A column at 1e-170 squares to zero and reads as gradient-free (infinite variance) although its physical esd is ordinary.
evidence: arithmetic: 2^-400 = 3.9e-121 squares to 1.5e-241, a normal double; 1/d^2 stays under 1e241 (docstring, WP-1463)
note: Inside the window the arithmetic is untouched, so an ordinary fit is bit-identical. Any exponent up to ~511 would serve.

name: rietx.optimize.statistics.MAX_SHIFT_CONVERGED
decides: McCusker et al.'s convergence band: max shift/esd <= 0.1 in the final cycle.
evidence: McCusker et al. (1999) J. Appl. Cryst. 32, 36, § 7 (docstring; paper not on disk)
note: No src code reads it: only tests (test_joint_report.py, test_refine_synthetic.py, test_skill_claims.py) and a schema docstring (grep 2026-10-19). The statistics.py comment says it 'sets the level of one report sentence'; nothing does. A declared name with no reader, in the sense of CLAUDE.md 'a declared name is a claim'.

name: rietx.schemas.results.Statistics.esd_inflation
decides: Multiplies every reported esd by sqrt(S''/S), Bérar & Lelann's serial-correlation factor, always on.
without: Esds at chi2_red * (J^T J)^-1 only, the form GSAS-II and FullProf print; every esd smaller by the factor: 2.15 on FAP lab, 8.07 on NAC synchrotron, 7.1-10.2 on WP-1417's synchrotron fits before v1.6 lowered it 12-21 %, 1.13 on perfectly white residuals.
evidence: Bérar & Lelann (1991) J. Appl. Cryst. 24, 1, § IV eqs 10-12 (docstring; paper not on disk, formula not re-derived); not GSAS-II's or FullProf's default (checked)
judgement: fails. Dissenter: a refiner quoting or comparing esds under the convention GSAS-II and FullProf print (sqrt(chi2_red) scaling only), e.g. checking a cell against another code or a referee's expectation; and one whose misfit is a systematic profile error, where serial correlation is the model's fault and an inflated esd is a guess at it. The package's own gate refuses the inflated esd as evidence (refine.py:1655-1665: a present phase read as absent, 0.23 sigma by the reported esd against 2865 sigma by counting noise).
note: GSAS-II 5.8.4 never mentions it: grep of *.py for Berar, Lelann, serial and Durbin finds only the Durbin-Watson statistic computed (GSASIIstrMath.py:4995) and printed (GSASIIstrIO.py:3633), never applied; its esds are covMatrix = result[1]*GOF**2 (GSASIIstrMain.py:397, checked). FullProf's manual gives sigma = a_k*sqrt(A^-1_kk * chi2_nu) (§ 3.10, eq 3.7, checked), cites Bérar & Lelann only in its bibliography, and the fp2k binary prints 'A better estimate of the accuracy of structural parameters is obtained multiplying sigmas by the parameter SCOR' with a Bérar line beside it (strings, checked): reported, not applied; whether a PCR switch applies it is unchecked. TOPAS unchecked. rietx's own VALIDATION.md says XND applies the same Bérar factor (not checked). Case for keeping (the strongest): the factor is cited, XND applies it, three consumers rest on it (N/f^2 in the delta-BIC penalty, WP-1417; the moment-angle test scale, least_squares.py:841; the CIF export text, io/exporters.py:443-460) and a demotion that reports the chi2_red-scaled esd as the esd with f beside it would move every esd by 1.13 to 8. Evidence the factor does not make esds cover truth: SRM 660c a = 4.156882(21) against the certificate-derived 4.156780 is 4.9 sigma (VALIDATION.md:287-291, interim band; arithmetic mine). Not scale-invariant: z_i reads a_i^2, so the factor grows with chi2_red at fixed correlation (the paper intends it). Provenance: WP-0407 (placement), #674 (eqs 10-12, v1.6, factor 2.71 -> 2.15 FAP, 9.25 -> 8.07 NAC). Tier 2 is for the cited statistic; the action fails the ground.

name: rietx.optimize.statistics.normal_factors:chi2_red_scaling
decides: Scales the covariance by chi2_red = sum r^2/(N-P), including when chi2_red < 1 (esds shrink).
without: Esds from (J^T J)^-1 alone, which are right only if the weights are exact.
evidence: GSAS-II 5.8.4 GSASIIstrMain.py:397 covMatrix = result[1]*GOF**2: same default (checked); FullProf manual eq 3.7: same (checked)
judgement: none: GSAS-II and FullProf both scale by chi2_red by default (checked); TOPAS unchecked. Whole-pattern chi2_red < 1 means the file's esds are pessimistic and shrinking is the standard reading (statistics.py docstring).
note: chi2_floor=True (max(chi2_red, 1)) is a caller option for per-peak profile fits, default off (caller). The Bérar factor multiplies this, so on a chi2_red = 2 pattern the esd is sqrt(2)*f times the counting esd. FullProf computes chi2_nu over points with Bragg contributions only, rietx over all N.

name: rietx.optimize.statistics.normal_factors:jacobi_equilibration
decides: Scales the normal matrix to unit diagonal before the pseudo-inverse, so no parameter's units set the cut.
without: The largest column sets the pinv cutoff for all: on NAC 4 of 17 directions were zeroed and phases.0.gauss_size read 6.1e-14 +- 9.9e-11 where the equilibrated inverse gives +- 4.3e8 (WP-1110 item 14).
evidence: GSAS-II 5.8.4 GSASIImath.GSASIImath.py HessianLSQ 269-271 and 433-434 (Adiag, Anorm): same, always (checked); van der Sluis (1969) Numer. Math. 14, 14 (docstring)
judgement: none: scaling by sqrt(diag) leaves the covariance unchanged in exact arithmetic and only fixes which directions the cut names; GSAS-II does it unconditionally (checked). An esd must not depend on another parameter's units (measured 2x before, 4e-16 after, on a synthetic 400x4 problem).

name: rietx.optimize.statistics._psd_pinv:magnitude_inversion
decides: Inverts every kept eigenvalue by its magnitude, so a rounding-level negative eigenvalue of a PSD matrix is not a negative variance.
without: Six undetermined LaB6+cBN Lorentzian widths read '+- 0.000' and HIGH_CORRELATION fell silent, split by platform (eigenvalues -3.5e-15 to +3.7e-15 of the largest).
evidence: arithmetic: a PSD matrix has no negative eigenvalue, so the sign is rounding; bit-identical to pinv when none is negative (WP-1930)
judgement: none: no competent refiner wants a negative variance floored to an esd of exactly 0.

name: rietx.optimize.least_squares.run_least_squares:ftol
decides: The solver's relative cost-decrease tolerance, 1e-9, which StageSpec.ftol=None resolves to on the last stage.
without: At scipy's 1e-8 a stage stops sooner; WP-1123 measured 1e-6 on intermediate stages at <=0.03 esd (cpd-1a, cpd-2, trigger).
evidence: WP-1113/1123: expensive stages terminate on ftol; the tail below 1e-6 banks <=0.03 esd; the 1e-9 itself has no stated source (scipy's default is 1e-8)
provenance: WP-1113 and WP-1123 measured the cost of running down to 1e-9 on cpd-1a, cpd-2 and the trigger protocol (macOS arm64, 2026-08-21); the value 1e-9 predates them.
families: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin (cpd-1a, cpd-2, trigger: one family), verifies
failure_case: none stated for 1e-9; the record's case is the looser value: 1e-6 on every stage but the last moved a degenerate instrument-X/lor_size direction by a nominal 1.2 esd (WP-1123).
judgement: none: a convergence tolerance on a stage is not a decision about the caller's model; the final stage's tightness is what the answer is read at.
note: Third and fourth spellings of the same literal: run_multi_least_squares (least_squares.py:2606) and lm.minimize (lm.py:360, with max_nfev=400 = 100*4 at :359). The rietx value is tighter than TRF's 1e-8 and GSAS-II's 'min dM/M' 0.001 (GSASIIobj.py:20, checked), different quantities (GSAS-II's is the relative chi2 change between cycles). intermediate_ftol (1e-6) is strategy/staged.py's row.

name: rietx.optimize.least_squares.run_least_squares:max_iter
decides: Iterations a stage may spend (budget max_iter*4 evaluations), 100.
without: A diverging pattern spent ten minutes before the old n_params multiplier was retired (WP-1109).
evidence: answer-invariant for a converging stage: runaway guard (WP-1109, 'never a timer'); no test asserts the margin
note: Sibling spelling in run_multi_least_squares (least_squares.py:2606). The seat default of max_iter on Stage/PlanSpec is another reader's row. GSAS-II 'max cyc' defaults to 3 cycles (GSASIIobj.py:20, checked), a different quantity (outer Gauss-Newton cycles).

name: rietx.optimize.least_squares._feasible_start:trf_nudge
decides: TRF requires a strictly feasible start, so it is moved 1e-12 off any bound it sits on (the LM driver is handed it on the bound).
evidence: arithmetic: scipy TRF needs a start strictly inside the bounds; 1e-12 is absolute and sub-resolution for any width of order 1e-3 or larger (WP-1937)
note: Absolute, not relative. Reached only with solver='trf' (caller). Equals XTOL, which scipy uses as the rtol of its active_mask (clash note).

name: rietx.optimize.least_squares._DegenerateCellGuard:penalty_factor
decides: On a DegenerateCellError a trial returns 10x the last evaluated residual so the driver rejects it.
without: The stage would crash on a trial the search would have rejected itself (#283).
evidence: answer-invariant: any factor > 1 makes the trial a rejection (LM raises lambda, TRF cuts the radius to 0.25*step, neither reads the size); tests/test_issue_283_cell_bounds.py
note: StageResult.n_degenerate_cell_probes records every probe (existing row). Not asserted that the factor is irrelevant; inferred from the two drivers' acceptance rules.

name: rietx.optimize.least_squares._freeze_cell_windows
decides: Bounds the cell of every phase with phase_support under PHASE_SUPPORT_SIGMA (3) to +-5 % / +-2 deg of its stage-start value (params/vector.py CELL_WINDOW_*).
without: A phase the data cannot see walks its cell down a flat direction (5.2 -> 25.6 Å at Rwp 0.0415, status converged; 81.9 Å with the window disabled on the same construction).
evidence: WP-1110: the runaway 5.2 -> 25.6 Å unbounded, ~5.0 Å windowed; windowing every cell regressed the chained IUCr suite; NAC refined values bit-identical 44 of 44
provenance: WP-1110 § The cell window, measured (cpd-1c chained IUCr suite, NAC two-phase protocol); WP-1301 and WP-1523 moved the screen.
families: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin (qarr), verifies (against the unbounded run)
APS 11-BM NAC, verifies (bit-identical)
failure_case: Windowing every phase's cell regressed the chained IUCr suite (cpd-1c): a quarter of an ångström inside a ±5 % window it never touches.
judgement: likely none for the hold it duplicates; open for the bound. Two acts on one cell: the absent-phase hold (refine, WP-1301, freezes every free structural path of a phase under 3 sigma of counting noise) and this window. A caller who wants the cell of a just-appearing phase free, start >5 % off its true cell, would see it trapped. Not measured here.
note: Constants live in params/vector.py (CELL_WINDOW_FRACTION 0.05, CELL_WINDOW_PAD_A 0.05, CELL_WINDOW_ANGLE_DEG 2.0) and model/forward.py:344 (PHASE_SUPPORT_SIGMA 3.0), another reader's. WP-1110's text says the window covers phases under 1 sigma; the constant is 3.0 now (possible drift after WP-1523, unverified). A caller's own finite bound suppresses the window on that side (cell_window docstring). Joint fits call _freeze_cell_windows_multi (:2311), windowing only where every histogram is under the cut. Third protection on the same columns: refine.clamp_cell_runaway (post-solve, always).

name: rietx.optimize.least_squares._freeze_strain_cap
decides: Caps lor_strain / gauss_strain where the term's own FWHM at the highest theta equals the fitted 2-theta range; armed only on terms that already reached it.
without: A strain term runs away until the phase is a second background; Rwp can improve while it does.
evidence: physics: a line wider than the interval it was measured over is not a line; STRAIN_CAP_RANGE_FRACTION = 1.0, 'deliberately not calibrated to any material' (params/vector.py:722)
judgement: none: no competent refiner reads a Lorentzian strain width larger than the whole scan as strain.
note: Bit-identical to an uncapped build where no term reaches it (hysteresis STRAIN_CAP_ARM_RTOL 1e-6, params/vector.py:730). Constants are another reader's. In a joint fit the widest cap governs (:2218). Also acts on the columns the Stephens cone and the lor_strain lock act on (clash notes). No record field names it; the bound test (BOUND_HIT / at_bound) is the only trace.

name: rietx.optimize.least_squares._freeze_size_cap
decides: Caps lor_size / gauss_size so a crystallite cannot fall below 2 nm (SIZE_CAP_MIN_SIZE_A = 20 Å, Scherrer K 0.9), armed only on a term that already reached it.
without: A size term runs to a crystallite of ~0.7 nm, under two unit cells, which is a placeholder and not a measurement.
evidence: params/vector.py:898 docstring: a runaway fence a couple of unit cells below anything in 606 solved TOPAS refinements (private corpus, cited by number)
provenance: params/vector.py:898 docstring: 606 solved TOPAS refinements, one source (one family); the smallest well-determined refined size is ~33 nm.
families: private TOPAS archive of 606 refinements (one source, one family), verifies (another code's results)
failure_case: 'Genuinely nanocrystalline specimens reach a few nm and must refine freely' (docstring); the cap is the 2 nm figure, deliberately permissive.
judgement: a dissenter exists: a refiner of sub-2 nm clusters or ultra-small nanoparticles would see the width pinned at the cap; the bound shows as at_bound and BOUND_HIT, so it is visible but it is still an action on their model.
note: Constants are another reader's. Written in params/vector.py as 'tier-1 bound' in the freezer's docstring (_longest_line_wavelength), but the 2 nm is an archive-derived value, not physics: the tier-1 label there does not hold. In a joint fit the widest cap is intersected onto the shared column (:2288, WP-1131). The longest emission line sets lambda.

name: rietx.optimize.blocked._Arrow.largest_eigenvalue:lanczos_tol
decides: Lanczos tolerance for lambda_max of the equilibrated arrow above _DENSE_EIGEN_MAX columns.
evidence: answer-invariant: 1e-6 relative places the PINV_RCOND cut, 'since it only places the cut' (docstring); no test yet
note: A 1e-6 relative error in lambda_max moves the cut 1e-6 relative; a direction within that of the cut could flip.

name: rietx.optimize.qpa._formula_units:tol
decides: Tolerance within which a per-element cell count must sit of a positive integer for Z to be the GCD (else Z = 1).
evidence: answer-invariant for fitted values: ZMV = cell_mass*V does not depend on Z; Z only sets ZMV.z, molar_mass and the exported _cell_formula_units_Z; no test yet
note: Second spelling of 0.02 in io/cif/blocks.py:301 (_reduces). qpa.py:163 reads it; weight_fractions uses cell_mass*V (qpa.py:156-169).

name: rietx.optimize.qpa.brindley_tau:series_switch
decides: |u| under 0.05 takes the Taylor series of Brindley's tau, otherwise the closed form (cancels near u = 0).
evidence: arithmetic: at |u| = 0.05 the series error is 1.0e-9 and the closed form's cancellation error 1.1e-12 (computed this session) against Brindley's ~1 % scatter
note: Reached only when the caller supplies particle_radius_um (caller). The series polynomial coefficients (0.75, 0.3, 1/12, 1/56) are arithmetic.

name: rietx.params.bodies.TORSION_STILL_TOL
decides: Refuses a rigid-body torsion whose axis is shorter than 1e-6 A, or whose moved atoms all lie within 1e-6 A of the axis line.
without: NaN on every atom of the body (zero-length axis), or a torsion whose column is identically zero
evidence: numerical floor: guards the division by the axis length and a zero Jacobian column; 1e-6 A is far below any structural distance
note: Not derived from eps; it is a refusal at declaration, so it can only move a number by refusing a model whose atoms sit < 1e-6 A from the axis.

name: rietx.params.bodies._DEG
evidence: arithmetic: degrees to radians

name: rietx.params.derived._DEG
evidence: arithmetic: degrees to radians

name: rietx.params.parametric.FORM_TEST_LEVEL
decides: Confidence level of the parametric-form test: a declared equation is flagged rejected when its statistic passes the chi-squared point at this level.
without: No rejected flag on a declared form, or a different false-rejection rate (1 in 20 per declaration at 0.95)
evidence: Venzon & Moolgavkar (1988) Appl. Statist. 37, 87 for the profile-likelihood cut; the 95 % level is convention, = PARAMETER_INTERVAL_LEVEL (docstring)
note: Inherits PARAMETER_INTERVAL_LEVEL with no free factor. The test acts on a caller-declared parametric equation only, and only reports (ParametricFormTest.rejected). No multiplicity correction across declarations; the docstring says so.

name: rietx.params.parametric.RANK_RTOL
decides: Relative size of a pivoted-QR diagonal of the column-normalised design matrix under which a basis direction is refused as absent.
without: A declared basis with a collinear direction would reach the fit and return a coefficient with no esd
evidence: numerical floor: sqrt(PINV_RCOND) = 3.2e-8, the R diagonal at which the covariance's pinv would discard the direction anyway (docstring derivation)
note: Inherits optimize.statistics.PINV_RCOND (1e-15, numpy's pinv default; optimize/statistics.py:52). Its tier is whoever tiers PINV_RCOND (WP-2002 reader for optimize/). Exact collinearity sits at ~1e-16, eight decades below.

name: rietx.params.vector.CELL_MIN_LENGTH_A
decides: Floor (A) on the default cell-length window, and the length under which a positive cell length is left alone rather than windowed.
without: A window could reach lengths no crystal has (the floor was 0.1 A before WP-1110)
evidence: TOPAS-Academic v8 Technical Reference s2.17 Table 2-1, Max(1.5, ...) (docstring; WP-1110 quotes the same table)
note: GSAS-II sets no default bounds (WP-1110 notes Controls['parmMinDict'] is user-supplied), so only TOPAS stands behind it. Only matters for a phase the data cannot see.

name: rietx.params.vector.CELL_WINDOW_PAD_A
decides: Additive pad (A) in the default per-stage cell-length window, so a small cell is not held tighter than a large one.
without: A small cell would get an absolute window narrower than a large one
evidence: TOPAS-Academic v8 Technical Reference s2.17 Table 2-1: 0.995*Val - 0.05 .. 1.005*Val + 0.05 (docstring; WP-1110)
note: Same pad as TOPAS. The fraction beside it is rietx's own (CELL_WINDOW_FRACTION).

name: rietx.params.vector.CELL_WINDOW_FRACTION
decides: Fraction of its starting value a cell length may travel within one stage, for a phase the data cannot see.
without: An unseen phase's cell can run to thousands of A (39 293 A seen on a 68-pattern in-situ series) until generate_reflections refuses
evidence: WP-1110: TOPAS's 0.5 %/iteration scaled to a stage (5 %); widest honest stage move 2.8e-4 on 11-BM NAC + SRM 660c (180x inside)
provenance: WP-1110 § The cell window, measured: 51 stage transitions of 11-BM NAC and SRM 660c (worst move 2.8e-4, median 9.2e-8); synthetic LaB6 started 1 % and 3 % wrong; IUCr round-robin cpd-1c (window on a visible phase cost 82 -> 400 iterations, corundum 9.04 vs 6.30 wt %); 68-pattern in-situ series (runaway to ~39 000 A).
families: APS 11-BM NAC and SRM 660c (one laboratory and instrument): verifies, survey of moves only, no certified bound
IUCr QPA round robin cpd-1c (laboratory XRD): verifies, own-result recovery unchanged to every digit
multi-phase in-situ series, 68 patterns (the runaway that motivated it): a failure case, not a reference
synthetic LaB6: verifies
failure_case: Started 3 % wrong the fit fails on its own (Rwp 0.96): the basin, not the window, is the obstacle. Windowing every phase broke cpd-1c, so it is restricted to phases phase_support judges unseen.
note: The 5 % is 10x TOPAS's per-iteration number, and the ten is rietx's own factor. After the WP-1301 hold (refine.py:1175, called at :3946) has set vary False on an unseen phase's cell, ParameterTable.bounds() (vector.py:3769) windows free entries only, so this window may be inert on the single-fit path; the lead should measure whether any path still binds it. See notes.md clash 1.

name: rietx.params.vector.CELL_WINDOW_ANGLE_DEG
decides: Degrees a cell angle may travel within one stage, for a phase the data cannot see.
without: An unseen phase's cell angle can run to the 1-179 deg clip
evidence: WP-1110: TOPAS's +-0.2 deg per iteration scaled by the same ten as the length window (2.0 deg); no angle survey in the record
provenance: WP-1110 § The cell window: shape from TOPAS (angles Val +- 0.2); the measurements in the record are on cell lengths (11-BM NAC/SRM 660c, synthetic LaB6). No angle was measured.
families: APS 11-BM NAC and SRM 660c: lengths only, verifies
failure_case: none stated for angles
note: Weakest of the window numbers: scaled by analogy, not measured.

name: rietx.params.vector.CELL_SAFETY_FRACTION
decides: Fraction of the stage's starting value a free cell length may end at before refine.clamp_cell_runaway pulls it back after the solve.
without: A supported phase can run away unseen (4.1566 -> 3803 A in twenty TRF iterations of one stage on a two-phase LaB6 reproduction) and crash the next stage's generate_reflections
evidence: WP-1110/#385: 15 % chosen as 3x the stage window; thermal expansion and composition are a few % at most; honest worst stage move 2.8e-4
provenance: WP-1110 (51-transition survey, 11-BM NAC/SRM 660c) and the 2026-09-17 reproduction on a synthetic two-phase LaB6 pattern with a 2 % trace copy at the same cell; review of #385.
families: APS 11-BM NAC and SRM 660c: verifies, moves only
synthetic two-phase LaB6 (the runaway reproduction): a failure case
multi-phase in-situ series (68 patterns): the original failure
failure_case: A cell tied to a caller's free vars.X is a moving path, not a free column, so it is never clamped; it is named by CELL_RUNAWAY (refine._vars_driven_cell_escapes) instead.
note: Dissenter for the clamp this constant drives: a breathing MOF or hydrate whose true cell is more than 15 % from the stage's start. WP-1110 measured that a fit 3 % off cannot converge anyway, and the pull-back is reported (CELL_RUNAWAY), so the clamp costs no answer the solver could reach. Action itself is refine.clamp_cell_runaway (another reader's).

name: rietx.params.vector.CELL_SAFETY_ANGLE_DEG
decides: Degrees a free cell angle may end at from its stage start before the post-solve clamp pulls it back (3.0 x CELL_WINDOW_ANGLE_DEG).
without: As CELL_SAFETY_FRACTION, for angles
evidence: WP-1110/#385: 3x the stage angle window, the 3 is a free factor with no angle measurement; inherits the tier-3 base
provenance: Same as CELL_SAFETY_FRACTION; the factor 3.0 is a threshold of its own, and no angle was surveyed.
families: APS 11-BM NAC and SRM 660c: lengths only
failure_case: As CELL_SAFETY_FRACTION (vars.X-driven cells escape the clamp)

name: rietx.params.vector._ANGLE_MIN_DEG
decides: Lower clip of a cell-angle window (deg), inside the 0 deg singularity of the metric tensor.
without: A window could reach a degenerate cell
evidence: arithmetic: the metric tensor is singular at 0 deg and 180 deg; the 1 deg margin is inert for any crystal (real cell angles 60-120 deg)
note: The 1 deg margin has no derivation. It binds only if a window edge (value +- 2 deg or +- 6 deg) crosses 1 deg, i.e. a cell angle already under 3 deg or 7 deg.

name: rietx.params.vector._ANGLE_MAX_DEG
decides: Upper clip of a cell-angle window (deg), inside the 180 deg singularity.
evidence: arithmetic: the metric tensor is singular at 180 deg; the 1 deg margin is inert for any crystal
note: As _ANGLE_MIN_DEG.

name: rietx.params.vector.STRAIN_CAP_RANGE_FRACTION
decides: Fraction of the fitted 2-theta span that one strain term's own FWHM may reach at the highest theta.
without: lor_strain exceeded 1 in 133 of 248 patterns and peaked at 1.1e5 on issue #140's CuO -> Cu series; covariance overflowed in 179 of 248
evidence: arithmetic: a line wider than the interval it was measured over carries no information; the 1.0 is the interval itself, no free factor (docstring)
note: Cap is ~80 deg on a 10-80 deg scan, 278x TOPAS's 0.3. WP-1130 measured strain_cap(14,70) = 79.98 against a real runaway of 10.37: the cap would not have bitten it. It binds only the extreme runaway. Evidence of the runaway is one series.

name: rietx.params.vector.STRAIN_CAP_ARM_RTOL
decides: Relative closeness to the cap at which it arms (hysteresis against TRF stopping a hair inside its bound).
evidence: numerical floor: 1e-6 sits eight decades above the ~1e-14 feasibility offset and far under any deliberate move; hysteresis pinned by test_strain_cap.py:160
note: Not derived from eps. Any value in about 1e-12..1e-3 gives the same behaviour; a smaller one disarms the cap on the stage after it fired.

name: rietx.params.vector._BACKSTOP_THETA_MAX_DEG
decides: Highest theta (deg) at which a strain or size range backstop is evaluated, off the 2-theta = 180 deg pole of tan and cos.
evidence: numerical floor: pole guard at 2theta = 180 deg; moves no number for any pattern ending below 2theta = 178 deg

name: rietx.params.vector.SIZE_CAP_RANGE_FRACTION
decides: The strain rule's fraction reused for size: a size term's FWHM at the highest theta may reach this share of the fitted span.
evidence: arithmetic: same information limit as STRAIN_CAP_RANGE_FRACTION, no free factor; on any real scan the 2 nm floor binds first (4 vs 54 deg on Cu 10-80)

name: rietx.params.vector.SIZE_CAP_ARM_RTOL
decides: Relative closeness to the size cap at which it arms (hysteresis).
evidence: numerical floor: as STRAIN_CAP_ARM_RTOL; hysteresis pinned by test_strain_cap.py:414

name: rietx.params.vector.SIZE_CAP_MIN_SIZE_A
decides: Smallest crystallite (A) a free size term may reach: a ceiling of (180/pi)*K*lambda/L on lor_size (3.97 deg at Cu Ka), armed once the term reaches it.
without: Size term runs away; the covariance overflows as for strain (same geometry)
evidence: v1.2 width fence: 2 nm, two cells under the private TOPAS archive's smallest well-determined size (33 nm of 606 refinements)
provenance: Set with the v1.2 width check (recorded in WP-1130 § folded from 1131); 606 solved TOPAS refinements, the private archive cited by number; the failure geometry is issue #140's 248-pattern series. A contributor's '4 deg/cos(theta)' figure (Michael).
families: private TOPAS archive, 606 refinements (one source): the corpus said nothing below 2 nm that was not exploratory; verifies, no reference value
failure_case: A genuinely sub-2-nm specimen (an ultrasmall nanoparticle) is pinned at 2 nm and reports BOUND_HIT; a finite stored max switches the cap off (tests/test_strain_cap.py:422).
note: One family, so it fails the mechanical ground as written; the docstring calls it 'deliberately permissive'. Companion flag SIZE_UNUSUALLY_SMALL (refine.SIZE_FLAG_SIZE_A = 50 A) already reports the believable band, so the cap is the runaway fence only.

name: rietx.params.vector._MOMENT_REFRAME_TOL
decides: Distance a magnetic moment frame may move between stages before ParameterTable.reframe_moments rebuilds it.
evidence: numerical floor: ~4.5e3 eps, above roundoff; a frame moved 1e-12 moves the moment by 1e-12 of its modulus (docstring)
note: Changing it moves cost and, below 1e-12 relative, no reported number. No test asserts that invariance; if the lead prefers class 'invariant' it needs one.

name: rietx.params.vector._SIGMA_MAX
decides: Largest esd whose square is still a float64; past it a physical esd is read as unmeasured.
without: An esd squared would overflow to inf in the covariance rescale (WP-1463)
evidence: numerical floor: sqrt(float64 max) from np.finfo (the floating-point format itself)

name: rietx.params.vector._SIZE_CAP_SCHERRER_K
decides: Scherrer constant used inside size_cap's physics floor.
evidence: Scherrer (1918); Langford & Wilson (1978) J. Appl. Cryst. 11, 102 tabulate K 0.89 (sphere FWHM) to 1.07 (integral breadth) (docstring of caglioti.SCHERRER_K)
note: A deliberate second spelling of model.profiles.caglioti.SCHERRER_K (0.9), pinned equal by tests/test_strain_cap.py:556. Reader M tiers the original. K moves the cap by 10-20 % with crystallite shape.

name: rietx.schemas.fraction.FRACTION_PROFILE_DCHI2
decides: Delta chi-squared for one parameter at 95 % (1.96^2), scaled by chi2_red and the Berar-Lelann factor squared, that makes a pinned width admissible.
evidence: Venzon & Moolgavkar (1988) Appl. Statist. 37, 87: profile-likelihood cut at the chi-squared(1) 95 % point (docstring)
note: A literal 3.84, not computed from PARAMETER_INTERVAL_LEVEL (chi2.ppf(0.95,1) = 3.8415): two spellings of one 95 % convention. Read only inside profile_fraction, which no default path calls.

name: rietx.schemas.fraction.FRACTION_PROFILE_EXCESS
decides: Multiple of the esd's own 95 % half-width an admissible fraction must lie beyond before QPA_FRACTION_UNDETERMINED fires.
without: The diagnostic would fire on a profile that merely confirms the esd, or stay silent on a two-basin fit
evidence: WP-1320: chosen, not measured; between controls (0.46, 0.67, 0.79) and a synthetic two-basin fixture (~75)
provenance: WP-1320: one synthetic trace-phase fixture (two basins, excess ~74) and three recipe-grid controls plus the 200 C-shaped control, all synthetic; the filer's real data (#203) is not in the repo.
families: synthetic two-basin fixture and controls (tests/test_qpa_multimodal.py): verifies, no reference
failure_case: none stated
note: Gates a diagnostic's existence (WP-2005's kind) inside a verb the caller invokes (grep 2026-10-19: Refinement.profile_fraction is called by no default path; refine.py:8664 only names it in a suggestion). If the lead treats every constant read only inside a caller-invoked verb as 'caller', this follows.

name: rietx.schemas.fraction.FRACTION_PROFILE_FWHM_MIN
decides: Smallest nonzero FWHM (deg 2theta) on the default width grid of profile_fraction.
evidence: pick verb: profile_fraction() no default path calls it (grep 2026-10-19); grid start below a lab instrument's own width
note: Chosen coarse grid; the profile is a scan, not a solve. Moves the reported range (an inner bound), so not answer-invariant.

name: rietx.schemas.fraction.FRACTION_PROFILE_N_FWHM
decides: Number of log-spaced widths on the default grid of profile_fraction.
evidence: opt-in: Refinement.profile_fraction(), no default path calls it (grep 2026-10-19)
note: 11 steps, ~2.3x per step on an 85 deg range; a coarser grid can only narrow the reported range. Half the fitted span is the top, because a wider pin outruns the frozen windows (FROZEN_COMPILE_STALE fired at 85 deg, not at 60).

name: rietx.schemas.interval.PARAMETER_INTERVAL_LEVEL
decides: Default confidence level of a profile interval (0.95); the chi-squared threshold follows from it.
evidence: Venzon & Moolgavkar (1988) Appl. Statist. 37, 87 for the interval; 95 % is the conventional level and the caller's argument (docstring)
note: Default of profile_interval(level=...), a verb no default path calls (grep 2026-10-19). Also read by params/parametric.py:58 (FORM_TEST_LEVEL) and optimize/least_squares.py:563. The convention is recalled, not checked; GUM (JCGM 100:2008) gives a 95 % coverage as the usual expanded uncertainty.

name: rietx.schemas.interval.PARAMETER_INTERVAL_MAX_REFITS
decides: Refits one side of a profile interval may spend before it stops and reports stop='refits'.
evidence: opt-in: Refinement.profile_interval(), no default path calls it (grep 2026-10-19)
note: Measured 6-10 refits a side on the synthetic fixture and 14-30 on the BT-1 neutron fit; 60 is twice the most. A budget guard: exhausting it leaves the end None with a stop reason, never a wrong end.

name: rietx.schemas.interval.PARAMETER_INTERVAL_SETTLE_RUNS
decides: Most refits one pinned value may take to settle (frozen peak windows recompile).
evidence: opt-in: Refinement.profile_interval(), no default path calls it (grep 2026-10-19)
note: Four, from a 22-value scan on BT-1 that stopped falling within three at every one. One neutron dataset.

name: rietx.schemas.interval.PARAMETER_INTERVAL_XTOL
decides: Tolerance an interval end is solved to, in units of the row's esd.
evidence: opt-in: Refinement.profile_interval(), no default path calls it (grep 2026-10-19)
note: 1e-3 esd is under two significant figures of the esd; moves the end's delta-chi2 by ~0.1 % of the threshold (docstring).

name: rietx.schemas.interval.PARAMETER_INTERVAL_CHI2_TOL
decides: Delta chi2 the interval treats as nothing, as a fraction of the threshold; sets settling and fit_is_minimum.
evidence: opt-in: Refinement.profile_interval(), no default path calls it (grep 2026-10-19)
note: Docstring: 'Chosen, not measured'; 1 % of the threshold is half a percent of the interval.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument._WAVELENGTH_MIN_A
decides: Strictly positive floor (A) for a wavelength Parameter.
without: A refined wavelength could reach zero, where the profile derivatives vanish
evidence: physics: lambda <= 0 puts every reflection at 2theta = 0; 1e-3 A is three orders under any diffraction wavelength (docstring)
note: A fence, not a claim about the instrument; wavelengths are held fixed by default.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.DEFAULT_HARMONIC_ORDER
decides: The order n a bare Harmonic() declares (lambda/2).
evidence: opt-in: Source.harmonics / NeutronSource.harmonics, default empty (grep 2026-10-19); the X-ray Source refuses a declared harmonic
note: Second order is the one a crystal monochromator normally passes with measurable intensity; a default, not a limit.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.HARMONIC_WEIGHT_SEED
decides: Seed (1 %) of a declared harmonic's relative weight.
evidence: opt-in: Harmonic declared by the caller, default off; seed below every reported beamline value so the fit has to travel
note: Validated only on NIST BT-1 (Gaultois et al. 2013, J. Phys.: Condens. Matter). Opt-in, one neutron family.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.HARMONIC_WEIGHT_MAX
decides: Ceiling (0.5) on a harmonic's weight.
evidence: opt-in: Harmonic declared by the caller, default off; hitting it is itself the finding (BOUND_HIT)
note: 'Not a tuning: a component over half the fundamental is not a contaminant of it'. No measurement behind 0.5.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument._DIFC_MIN
decides: Floor (1 us/A) on the time-of-flight calibration constant DIFC.
evidence: physics: DIFC = (m_N/h)(L1+L2)2 sin(theta) is strictly positive; 1 us/A is three orders under the smallest real bank (GEM bank 1, ~740)
note: TOF is read, never refined in this build (instrument.py:2240), so the floor is inert today.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.HUMP_FWHM_MIN
decides: Floor (0.1 deg 2theta) on a declared background hump's FWHM, off the Gaussian's pole at zero width.
evidence: opt-in: Instrument.extra_components, default empty; = STEPS_PER_FWHM_MIN (5) x 0.02 deg routine scan step (docstring)
note: Inherits STEPS_PER_FWHM_MIN = 5 (background/diagnostics.py:228, reader B); the 0.02 deg step is rietx's choice. Sits whole degrees under any real hump.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.EXTRA_PEAK_FWHM_MIN
decides: Floor (0.005 deg 2theta) on a declared sharp extra peak's FWHM.
evidence: opt-in: Instrument.extra_components, default empty; = STEPS_PER_FWHM_MIN (5) x 0.001 deg, the finest scan step tested (APS 11-BM Si 640c header)
note: No margin under a legitimate width: a peak narrower than five channels is a spike. One facility sets the step.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.EXTRA_PEAK_FWHM_MAX
decides: Default upper bound (0.5 deg) on a declared extra peak's FWHM; sizes its frozen window.
evidence: opt-in: Instrument.extra_components, default empty; a default for the window size, the caller widens it by saying so
note: Window half-width is window_fwhm_mult(eta.max)*fwhm.max + WINDOW_MIN_DEG, ~8 deg at the default.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument._ZERO_BOUND
decides: A stored lower bound at or under this is read as 'bound at zero' by the hump and peak width repairs.
evidence: numerical floor: 1e-12 is the value under which a stored min meant no bound before schema 0.46 (docstring)
note: Twin of structure._ZERO_BOUND. The repair it gates is a silent edit of a stored bound; see the new row for it.

name: rietx.schemas.structure._ZERO_BOUND
decides: A stored lower bound at or under this is read as 'bound at zero' by the March-Dollase r repair.
evidence: numerical floor: 1e-12 is the value under which a stored min meant no bound before schema 0.46 (docstring)
note: Twin of instrument._ZERO_BOUND (restated to keep the modules independent).

name: rietx.schemas.structure.MARCH_R_MIN
decides: Lower bound on the March-Dollase coefficient, off the pole at r = 0.
evidence: opt-in: Phase.preferred_orientation, default None; floor 0.15 chosen after r underflowed to 0 on a 90 wt % NaCl mixture (WP-1028 (e))
note: If re-tiered 3: WP-1028 (e) measured on NaCl/Li2CO3 mixtures (a laboratory); WP-1028 s(i) ran the IUCr round robin, brucite r = 0.67 sits inside, so no failure case stated. The pole at 0 is physics (tier 1); 0.15 is not forced. Strongly oriented films (clays, rolled sheet) can need r under 0.15; BOUND_HIT/FLOOR_HIT reports it.

name: rietx.schemas.structure.MARCH_R_MAX
decides: Upper bound (6.0) on the March-Dollase coefficient.
evidence: opt-in: Phase.preferred_orientation, default None; 'a texture no powder mount produces' (WP-1028 (e)), no measurement behind 6
note: Same provenance as MARCH_R_MIN; the upper value was never the failure.

name: rietx.schemas.structure.MOMENT_FLOOR_MU_B
decides: Modulus (mu_B) under which a magnetic moment block is at its floor: held and reported unsupported.
without: A moment fitted to a paramagnetic pattern walks (2.12 -> -1.73 mu_B) on a flat direction
evidence: WP-1327: 1e-3 mu_B, three orders under the smallest resolvable ordered moment; measured on BT-1 LaMnO3 and Cr2WO6 only
provenance: WP-1327: GSAS-II tutorial Cr2WO6 (null returned 0.067 +- 1.02 mu_B, caught by the ratio rule, not the floor) and NIST BT-1 LaMnO3 50 K (3.54 +- 0.33 against ~3.7 published).
families: neutron CW magnetic: NIST BT-1 LaMnO3 and GSAS-II-tutorials Cr2WO6 (one facility, one technique): Cr2WO6's 2.35(2) bar is not met by either code, so verifies only
failure_case: Cr2WO6's null case is decided by the esd ratio, not the floor: 'The null is met by the ratio rule, not by the floor' (WP-1327).
judgement: none: a modulus at 1e-3 mu_B has no direction and a vanishing Jacobian column (|F_m|^2 goes as m^2); every refiner holds it, as the absent-phase hold. Only the threshold is on trial and it is a floor, not a tolerance.
note: Rare feature: one family on disk; the record (generality.md 'Where three families do not exist') keeps such a threshold at the measured value, tiered 3 with grounds that say so. Also read by sequential.py:905 (2003's reseed) and report/magnetic.py:288.

name: rietx.schemas.structure.RIGID_BODY_DRIFT_TOL
decides: Distance (A) a rigid body's stored atoms may sit from the body's map before RIGID_BODY_TEMPLATE_DRIFT refuses the table.
evidence: numerical floor: roundoff drift measured at <= 1e-14 A, tolerance 1e-6 A (docstring); refusing at it protects against a hand-edited body atom
note: Opt-in feature (Phase.rigid_bodies). Refusal, not a repair, because silently moving the atom back would undo the edit.

name: rietx.schemas.structure.RIGID_BODY_ROTATION_BOUND
decides: Default box (+-pi rad) on each component of a body's rotation increment.
evidence: arithmetic: the increment's Jacobian is singular only at |d omega| = 2 pi; +-pi per component keeps |d omega| <= pi*sqrt(3) < 2 pi (docstring, WP-1803 review)
note: Opt-in feature. The bound can bind on a body started more than pi from its target orientation; BOUND_HIT reports.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.Source:kind
decides: Discriminator tag of the X-ray source class.
evidence: arithmetic: a union tag, no value judgement
judgement: none: not a choice; it names the class.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.Source:polarization
decides: Starting value 0.5, held, in [0, 1], of the beam's sigma-polarised fraction K when a Source is built without one.
without: Lorentz-polarisation of a synchrotron beam (K ~ 0.99) would be wrong by a few percent at low angle until K is freed
evidence: physics: K = 0.5 is the unpolarised beam, P = K + (1-K)cos^2(2theta) = (1+cos^2 2theta)/2 (docstring; GSAS POLA convention)
judgement: A synchrotron or monochromated-beam user who builds Source(lines=...) by hand: K = 0.99 (APS 11-BM) or 1/(1+cos^2 2theta_m). The presets set K (debye_scherrer 0.99, bragg_brentano from the monochromator angle), so only the bare constructor meets 0.5.
note: Held (vary False) by default. A wrong K moved a refined Biso by 12 sigma while Rwp barely moved (WP-1311 item 2). The beam condition is a fact outside the pattern (kind 3), but 'unpolarised' is the null reading, so it is a starting value, not an action. The lead may ask for it to be required. GSAS-II's default for this field was not located.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.Source:kbeta
decides: Kbeta filtering undeclared (None).
evidence: arithmetic: None is 'no claim made', never 'no filter'; the contamination screen runs unchanged (docstring, WP-1445)
judgement: none: declining to state a fact the package cannot know is not an action.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.Source:dispersion
decides: Anomalous scattering f' + i f'' from the Cromer-Liberman table is applied to every X-ray phase unless Source.dispersion is set to None.
without: Every reflection of a species mis-scaled by ((Z+f')^2+f''^2)/Z^2 - 1 (-16 % ZnO at Cu Ka, +7 % CaF2); QPA RMS error 2.26 vs 0.62 wt % on the IUCr round robin (WP-1001)
evidence: GSAS-II 5.8.4 GSASIIstrIO.GetFprime: Cromer-Liberman f'/f'' applied to every X-ray histogram, no switch (checked); TOPAS/FullProf not checked
judgement: none for the physics: species and wavelength are all it needs. Two situations choose otherwise. A user reproducing a pre-v0.7 or another code's no-dispersion number sets dispersion=None, which says so through DISPERSION_NEGLECTED. A user within a few tens of eV of an edge, where the atomic table is wrong in principle, gets a refusal (12 of 1176 element x anode pairs, e.g. Eu, Ho at Cu Ka) and supplies measured overrides.
note: WP-1001 flipped the default on measurement (census of 1176 combinations, IUCr round robin). Passes the judgement ground because every competent refiner includes it and the exceptions have a switch and a record. Neutron sources have no dispersion channel (NeutronSource.dispersion is always None).

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.Source:harmonics
decides: No lambda/n harmonic declared (empty list).
evidence: physics/arithmetic: an X-ray Source refuses a declared harmonic (harmonics_supported False, f' shared across lines), so empty is the only legal value; off is exact
judgement: none: the field exists so the refusal can name its reason.
note: On NeutronSource (schemas/instrument.py:322) the same empty default is an opt-in, 'caller'.

name: rietx.schemas.pattern.PatternData.sig:poisson_fallback
decides: When a pattern carries no esd column the weights are sigma = sqrt(max(y, 1)).
without: No weights, so no chi-squared and no esd; the fit could not start
evidence: GSAS-II 5.8.4 imports/G2pwd_xye.py:172-185: no esd gives w = 1/y, w = 0 at y <= 0 (checked); TOPAS default 1/Max(Yobs,1) (recalled, not checked)
judgement: A refiner whose intensities are not counts (a rate, a normalised or background-subtracted pattern) would not take sqrt(y): sigma is then wrong by a constant factor, which rescales chi2 and the Berar-Lelann-corrected esds and leaves the fit alone except through the max(.,1) floor. The reader withholds sigma when the scale cannot be established (PATTERN_INTENSITY_SCALED), and DataRef.has_sigma / RefinementResult.weighted say whether sigma was measured. A point at y < 1 differs from GSAS-II (w = 1/y, or zero weight at y <= 0).
note: Always on, no switch. No field says which branch fired on a result (RefinementResult.sigma carries the numbers; project DataRef.has_sigma and textdoc's 'sigma from file' say it for projects). The floor at 1 is rietx's own, a numerical guard that does move reported numbers on low-count channels.

name: rietx.schemas.pattern._floor_sigma:relative_floor
decides: A zero or negative esd is raised to 1e-3 x the median positive esd, so no channel has infinite weight.
without: A zero esd gives weight infinity and the fit returns nan
evidence: #650 (relative floor) and WP-1952's inherited note (#897): a zero esd then weighs ~1e6x its neighbours; no source for the 1e-3
provenance: Set by #650 on a per-monitor reduction pattern (tests/test_schemas.py:437, one zero 'a gap the floor exists for'); WP-1952 Inherited records the failure on #897's two files with no diagnostic.
families: one normalised per-monitor reduction pattern (test fixture): verifies, not a reference
failure_case: WP-1952 Inherited (#897, 2026-10-13): a third column with one 0 is adopted as sigma and that point weighs about 1e6x its neighbours, with no diagnostic.
judgement: Shown a zero esd, two careful people differ: GSAS-II skips a negative esd and falls back to 1/y on a zero one (checked, imports/G2pwd_xye.py:176-185); the pdCIF reader drops a weight column with any zero (WP-1952 text); rietx floors at 1e-3 median. A competent refiner would not give one channel 1e6x the weight. The explanation (a gap, a blank, a dead channel) lies outside the pattern.
note: WP-1952 holds the open decision (floor, drop or refuse). Some value must be chosen for sigma <= 0, so 'report' here means a diagnostic naming the channels beside whatever safe choice remains. Shared by RefinementResult.sig (schemas/results.py:1700).

name: rietx.model.forward.compile_model:background_sigma_widening
decides: With a measured background that carries fixed_sigma, the channel weight becomes sigma^2 + s^2 sigma_f^2 at the scale the stage compiles at.
without: A short blank scan would weigh as heavily as a long one; the specimen's chi2 would ignore the blank's noise
evidence: arithmetic: variances of two independent counting measurements add (propagation of uncertainty); the curve's own statistics enter at the scale applied to it
judgement: none: every refiner who declares fixed_sigma wants it propagated; fixed_sigma=None (every estimator's output, a blank with no esd column) is the off state. The two caveats are named in the docstring (interpolation correlates neighbours, so the sigma is a lower bound; one blank reused across a series has fully correlated error).
note: Switch: the caller supplying fixed_sigma (BackgroundFixedPlusChebyshev.fixed_sigma, default None, schemas/instrument.py:1662). GSAS-II and TOPAS do not propagate a measured background's sigma that I know of (not checked); this is arithmetic, not practice. Frozen per stage, so a stage that moves the scale re-weights at the next compile (clash 5).

name: rietx.params.vector.cell_window
decides: Per-stage default bounds on the cell of a phase phase_support judges unseen: +-5 % (+0.05 A pad), +-2 deg, floored at 1.5 A and clipped to 1-179 deg; a finite stored bound wins per side.
without: An unseen phase's cell ran to 39 293 A on a 68-pattern in-situ series until generate_reflections refused, hundreds of stages downstream
evidence: WP-1110: shape from TOPAS s2.17 Table 2-1 (default cell bounds); window restricted to unseen phases after windowing all broke IUCr cpd-1c
provenance: WP-1110 § The cell window, measured. See CELL_WINDOW_FRACTION.
families: APS 11-BM NAC and SRM 660c: verifies
IUCr QPA round robin cpd-1c: verifies
68-pattern in-situ series: the failure that motivated it
failure_case: Windowing every phase regressed cpd-1c (corundum 9.04 vs 6.30 wt %) because TRF scales its trust region by the distance to the bounds, so the window is restricted to unseen phases.
judgement: none for the action: no competent refiner lets a phase the data cannot see refine its cell (the record's own absent-phase argument). A dissenter for the numbers is a caller who wants wider travel for a real but weak phase; a finite stored min or max outranks the window, and BOUND_HIT reports a window that bound (bounds() feeds bound_findings).
note: Overlaps the WP-1301 hold exactly: both read phase_support < PHASE_SUPPORT_SIGMA (least_squares.py:2194 vs refine.py:513). The hold runs first and sets vary False, and bounds() windows free entries only, so on the single-fit path this window may bind only where the hold leaves a cell free. Measure before keeping it. Clash 1.

name: rietx.params.vector.strain_cap_hi
decides: Per-stage upper bound on lor_strain (and its square on gauss_strain) = fitted 2theta span / tan(theta_max), armed only once the term has reached it; a finite stored max wins.
without: lor_strain exceeded 1 in 133 of 248 patterns (peak 1.1e5) on issue #140's CuO -> Cu series, starving a real 16 wt % phase below 1 wt % in 195 of 248 and returning esds above 100 wt % in 179
evidence: arithmetic: a line wider than the interval measured is not a line; tests/test_strain_cap.py:205 asserts the bound arrays are unchanged for a fit below the cap
judgement: none: a width exceeding the whole measured interval is degenerate with the background in every competent reading. The cap (~80 deg) is 278x TOPAS's 0.3 and 56x the STRAIN_UNUSUALLY_LARGE flag, so no believable strain meets it. A dissenter would be a refiner with a nanocrystalline or heavily defective phase far out in the tail, and the cap does not reach them.
note: Evidence of the runaway is one series (#140). WP-1130 measured strain_cap(14,70) = 79.98 against a real runaway of 10.37 and says the cap would not have bitten it, so it binds only at extreme runaway. Caller sees BOUND_HIT (bounds() read by check_guards). A free lor_strain of a phase the data cannot see is also held by the WP-1301 hold; clash 2.

name: rietx.params.vector.size_cap_hi
decides: Per-stage upper bound on lor_size (square on gauss_size) = min of a 2 nm Scherrer floor and the range backstop, armed only once the term reaches it; a finite stored max wins.
without: A size term runs to the 1/cos(theta) pole geometry as strain does (same runaway)
evidence: v1.2 width fence: 2 nm floor chosen under the private TOPAS archive's smallest well-determined size (33 nm of 606)
provenance: See SIZE_CAP_MIN_SIZE_A.
families: private TOPAS archive, 606 refinements (one source): verifies
failure_case: A real sub-2-nm specimen is pinned at 2 nm and reports BOUND_HIT; a finite stored max switches it off.
judgement: A refiner of ultrasmall nanoparticles (1-2 nm, the Debye-scattering border) would choose otherwise: a size of 15 A is a legitimate answer for them. They set a finite max on lor_size, which outranks the cap (tests/test_strain_cap.py:422), and see BOUND_HIT meanwhile. The record's own corpus found nothing under 2 nm that was not exploratory (a 0.69 nm 'crystallite' of Si).
note: The tier-1 part is the range backstop (same arithmetic as the strain cap); the 2 nm floor is the tier-3 part and decides on every real scan (4 vs 54 deg on Cu 10-80). SIZE_UNUSUALLY_SMALL (50 A) already reports the believable band, so demoting the cap to a report loses only the runaway fence. The lead should put the dissenter to the maintainer.

name: rietx.params.vector.tie_window
decides: Bounds a tie's source so the tied dependent stays inside the dependent's own declared limits, solved from lo <= coeff*s + offset <= hi (outer box when several sources).
without: A coefficient other than 1 carries a dependent past a physical limit (occ above 1.5, March r below its floor) with no bound seen by the solver
evidence: arithmetic: the interval that keeps an affine tie inside limits the caller already declared; TOPAS makes the user write it by hand (Coelho 2018 J. Appl. Cryst. 51, 210, docstring)
judgement: none: it only enforces two declarations the caller already made. A source held at a window it did not declare returns through bound_findings.
note: Last of four bounds in ParameterTable.bounds (vector.py:3789) by design: they do not commute. The docstring still says 'Biso in [0, 25]', stale since WP-1534 (2026-10-04) removed the Biso bounds.

name: rietx.params.vector.FLOOR_SEEDS
decides: Typical size per width unit (deg 1e-3, deg^2 1e-6, um^2 1e-3) that sizes the forward-difference step of a column bounded below at zero.
without: A width column at exactly 0 is differenced over an absolute step: 1.4e-3 error in v's column and 1.5e-2 in w's on LaB6 + cBN (11-BM), measured against jax
evidence: answer-invariant in intent: moves a finite-difference column's truncation, not the accepted answer; WP-1936 measured columns within 5e-7 of jax at FD_STEP 1e-6; no test asserts answer invariance yet
note: Read only by optimize/least_squares.py:1167 (_fd_typicals), which feeds the whole-model FD column the analytic branches do not cover. Measured on LaB6 + cBN (11-BM) and lab brucite. It changes the Jacobian at ~1e-7, so the converged answer moves within ftol, not bit-identically; the class needs a test that a 10x step change leaves accepted values within a stated bound.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument._KA_DOUBLETS
decides: Emission-line wavelengths of the six lab anodes (A), one measurement scale.
evidence: Hoelzer, Fritsch, Deutsch, Haertwig & Foerster (1997) Phys. Rev. A 56, 4554 (Cr, Fe, Co, Cu); Deslattes & Kessler (1985) (Mo, Ag) (docstring)
note: Data table in a dict, invisible to the walk. 'One column of one evaluation' is the claim; Cu pair pinned by tests (test_lab_instrument) to the SRM 660c scale. Bearden (1967) is a different scale (24-26 ppm for Mo, Ag).

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.TCHZ_BOUNDS
decides: Default refinement box per Caglioti/Lorentzian width (U in [-0.05, 1], V in [-0.5, 0.5], W in [1e-8, 1], X and Y in [0, 1]) for every X-ray preset.
without: Widths unbounded: U, V, W walk to a negative or implausible resolution (WP-1311 item 4: the ceiling permits a 1 deg instrument FWHM)
evidence: WP-1312/1938: the numbers every X-ray fit's search box has had; W's floor is the Gamma_G^2 clamp (1e-8, WP-1938 D7)
provenance: WP-1311 item 4 and WP-1312 (kept 2026-09-11: 'the bound stays'); box sized for a lab or synchrotron X-ray line. The W floor is arithmetic (WP-1938).
families: APS 11-BM, lab X-ray: sizes the box; no failure measured
failure_case: A CW neutron line (U = 1.576 on ILL D1B, issue #276) sits outside it; the constructor refuses a bare width and points to ProfileTCHZ.coarse.
judgement: A refiner of a coarser instrument (CW neutron, 0.2-2.5 deg lines) would choose otherwise; the schema refuses by name and offers TCHZ_BOUNDS_COARSE, and a refined width at a bound reports BOUND_HIT.
note: A dict, invisible to the walk. Default Parameter box, so it acts on every default X-ray fit that frees a width. Row for W's floor belongs to reader M (caglioti._MIN_GAMMA_G2).

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.TCHZ_BOUNDS_COARSE
decides: Coarse-instrument box (U in [-0.5, 8], V in [-4, 4], W in [1e-8, 8], X and Y in [0, 8]) used by constant_wavelength_neutron.
evidence: WP-1312: measured on the public APDW Co3O4 set (ILL D1B, 2.52 A, issue #276): converges to U = 1.654 +- 0.051, within 5 % of its FullProf model
provenance: WP-1312 / issue #276: one ILL D1B dataset against its FullProf model.

failure_case: none stated

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.TCHZ_DEFAULTS
decides: Starting values of the five width coefficients (u 0, v 0, w 1e-3, x 1e-3, y 0).
evidence: no source stated: seeds that keep the Gaussian width off its clamp (W) and the Lorentzian off zero (X); every stage's seed or the caller replaces them
provenance: no WP states them; inside the v0.1 schema
failure_case: none stated
judgement: none: a starting value a stage re-seeds or the data overrides; any start in the box reaches the same widths unless the basin is missed, which no record measures.

name: rietx.schemas.instrument.Instrument:zero_shift
decides: Starting value 0 and a box of +-0.5 deg on the zero shift.
without: A free zero shift is unbounded and correlates with the cell and displacement
evidence: no source stated for the +-0.5 deg; a runaway guard
provenance: No WP states the +-0.5 deg (searched docs/wp, 2026-10-19). The Geometry offsets' +-1 mm is WP-1311's, kept 'because it has stood since v0.2'.
failure_case: none stated
